// diagnostic E2808

Jet.RouteMethodTokenRefused

HTTP route method `{method}` is refused: {reason}.

What

HTTP route method `{method}` is refused: {reason}.

Why

A custom route method is an RFC 9110 token, kept in the exact case it is sent. A standard method spelled exactly registers with its own verb, so `custom` refuses it; one check runs on a static method while building and on a run-time method when its mux registers it.

Fix

Register a standard method with its own verb (`mux.get`), and give `custom` any other token of letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.RouteMethodTokenRefused: Tests/UI/http_route_custom_method.stderr.

Error: Jet.AmbiguousRoute: Two routes both match `PURGE /cache`.
  --> Tests/UI/http_route_custom_method.jet:30:9
    |
 30 |     mux.custom("PURGE", "/cache", handle)
    |         ^^^^^^
  --> Tests/UI/http_route_custom_method.jet:26:9
    |
 26 |     mux.custom("PURGE", "/cache", handle)
    |         ^^^^^^ first registered here
 Why: Pages, convention files, handler routes and marked methods share one route table, so two rows with one method and address make dispatch ambiguous and one of them would never be reached. A route added while the program runs is checked when it is added.
 Fix: Remove one of the two registrations, rename the convention file, or make the addresses distinct (e.g. mount one under its own prefix).
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.AmbiguousRoute

Error: Jet.RouteMethodTokenRefused: HTTPRouter custom route method must be a static String
  --> Tests/UI/http_route_custom_method.jet:35:19
    |
 35 |     router.custom(names[0], "/cache", handle)
    |                   ^^^^^^^^
 Why: Router and `#Server.Custom` routes are fully checked while building; only an App takes a run-time method, checked when it registers
 Fix: Use a literal or compile-time String constant, or register the route on a `web.app()`
